I have farmed for more than fifty years, and this small plot near my home is where I grow my beans and cowpea mixed in with the other crops. I will not buy chemical fertilizer for beans because they have always grown well here without it, and I will spread two wheelbarrows of goat manure instead since I own this land and the manure costs me nothing. I will use my own saved seed and depend on my sons and me to weed and harvest — about twenty days of family labor this season — because paying workers or buying spray is too much cash for such a small corner. We depend on the rains here in the North West, so I will not irrigate.
